answers.core: Because there is `move_to_front()`, which can be workarounded by ```get_parent().move_child(self, get_parent().get_child_count())``` but it is core, so why `move_to_back()` shouldn't be?
answers.workaround: There is a workaround: ```get_parent().move_child(self, 0)``` but it is not particularly convenient when there is ```move_to_front()```
